entities.summary: Andouin Aubert was a French jurist, bishop, and Cardinal who played a significant role in the development of canon law during the medieval period. He served as a member of the College of Cardinals, participating in the election of Pope Innocent VI in 1352. Aubert's legal expertise and clerical status allowed him to influence the development of ecclesiastical law, shaping the institution of the Catholic Church. As a bishop, he oversaw the administration of the Diocese of Sens in France, implementing reforms to improve the welfare of his flock. Aubert's legacy can be seen in the continued relevance of canon law in modern times, with his contributions to the field remaining a vital part of the Catholic Church's tradition. His impact on the institution of the Church and the development of canon law has been recognized by scholars, who continue to study his life and work as a testament to his enduring influence.
